clue.text: VIP oddly, oddly behind one not a VIP

indicators.note: one piece placed after the other in the answer

parts.note: a nob is a toff or bigwig, a very important person

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters (first, third, fifth) of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone muses on how strangely an important person sits behind a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'oddly' is the indicator and the second is its fodder: the odd letters of 'oddly' are O, D, Y, which go 'behind' NOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance or standing is called a nobody, the opposite of a bigwig.

clue.text: It gets a question of identification all sewn up

definitions.text: It gets a question of identification all sewn up

parts.words: It gets a question of identification all sewn up
parts.note: sewn up means settled, but literally this label is stitched into clothing to show whose they are

explanation.definitionFit: A name tape is a strip bearing the owner's name, sewn into school clothes.

clue.text: Get the chatter over

indicators.note: over signals turning the word round, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: gab is idle talk, chatter

explanation.surface: Stop the talking now.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something is to get or secure it, as in bagging a seat.

clue.text: Ruined citadel at the mouth of the Nile maybe

definitions.text: at the mouth of the Nile maybe

indicators.note: a ruined building has been knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crumbling fortress stands by the Nile's estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the mouth of the Nile maybe' is a descriptive phrase, matching an adjective; the Nile ends in a famous delta.
explanation.definitionFit: Deltaic means relating to a delta, the fan of land at a river mouth like the Nile's.

clue.text: Magicians struggle with security devices

parts.note: a war is a struggle or conflict
locks are devices that keep doors secure

explanation.surface: Wizards wrestle with padlocks and bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Warlocks are male witches or sorcerers, practitioners of magic.

clue.text: Disorganised like china after bull's visit?

definitions.meaning: a bull in a china shop smashes the crockery, leaving pieces strewn everywhere in the shop

explanation.surface: A mess like crockery after a bull has come into the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: All over the shop is British slang for chaotic or scattered everywhere.

clue.text: The way to eat dip in a dish

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the inner one, eating it

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
a sag is a dip or drooping

explanation.surface: The proper way to eat a dip from a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked dish of layered pasta sheets.

clue.text: In which one separates the tabs and bows

definitions.text: In which one separates the tabs and bows

parts.words: In which one separates the tabs and bows
parts.note: tabs are stage curtains in theatre slang; they part and the cast bows to the audience

explanation.definitionFit: A curtain call is the actors' return to the stage to take bows at the end of a show.

clue.text: Bit cut from middle of old Italian's rich fabric

indicators.note: a letter is removed from the centre of the word

parts.note: the Samnites were an ancient people of southern Italy

explanation.surface: A scrap is snipped from the middle of an old Italian's luxurious cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: SAMNITE has seven letters; 'Bit cut from middle of' removes its central N.
explanation.definitionFit: Samite is a heavy silk fabric, often interwoven with gold, worn in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: The very words Caesar might have said

definitions.text: The very words Caesar might have said

parts.words: The very words Caesar might have said
parts.note: the Latin phrase for exact wording, in the language a Roman would have spoken

explanation.definitionFit: Ipsissima verba is Latin for the precise words used, quoted exactly.

clue.text: Big city girl is going across a lake to swimming pool

indicators.note: the outer letters straddle the inner group, spanning it from side to side

parts.note: Meg is a girl's name, short for Margaret
taken as written
L is a standard abbreviation for lake on maps

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of the word pool are moving about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl from the big city crosses a lake on her way to the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges POOL into OPOL; with A and L that makes ALOPOL, which MEG and IS are 'going across'.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalopolis is a very large urban area or sprawling conurbation.

clue.text: Animal's memory

definitions.meaning: a male sheep is one such animal
random-access memory in a computer, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A creature's power of recall.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is a male sheep, and RAM is the working memory of a computer.

clue.text: Thauthage will give you masses of brains!

definitions.text: Thauthage will give you masses of brains!

parts.words: Thauthage will give you masses of brains!
parts.note: Thauthage is sausage said with a lisp; a lisped name for another sausage, the cured Italian one, gives the masses of grey matter in the brain

explanation.surface: A lisping butcher promises that his sausage will make you clever.
explanation.walkthrough: The lisp turns S into TH: the sausage SALAMI said with a lisp becomes the brain structures.
explanation.definitionFit: The thalami are the paired masses of grey matter deep within the forebrain.

clue.text: Salsa loudly, wildly, in a November event

indicators.note: dancing wildly suggests these letters are flung into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: People dance the salsa noisily and wildly at a November party.
explanation.definitionFit: All Souls' Day, on 2 November, is the Christian day for commemorating the dead.

clue.text: Against a handout for homeless person

parts.note: v, short for versus, means against
a grant is money handed out

explanation.surface: Someone argues against giving a handout to a rough sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a wanderer with no settled home, a tramp.

clue.text: Officer who may briefly offer a postscript?

definitions.text: Officer who may briefly offer a postscript?

parts.words: Officer who may briefly offer a postscript?
parts.note: a postscript at the foot of a letter is written PS, which is also the short form of this police rank

explanation.definitionFit: A police sergeant is a rank of officer above constable, abbreviated PS.

clue.text: One has this to say for the meaning of course

definitions.text: One has this to say for the meaning of course

parts.words: One has this to say for the meaning of course
parts.note: add the word to say and the phrase means of course, obviously

explanation.definitionFit: Needless to say is an idiom meaning of course, so the word completes it.

clue.text: Chemical with odour alchemist concocted

indicators.note: something concocted is mixed up, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: An alchemist brews something with a pungent smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium chlorate is a chemical compound used as a weedkiller and bleach.

clue.text: One copper in Avon struggling, lacking all context

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the metal symbol goes inside the rearranged river name
struggling suggests the letters of Avon are thrashing about out of order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A lone policeman flounders in the River Avon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' makes NVAO; 'copper' reads as a policeman in the surface but is the metal here.
explanation.definitionFit: In vacuo is Latin for in a vacuum, meaning isolated from any surrounding context.

parts.note: to tend is to nurse or care for

clue.text: Phone a girl in foreign city

parts.note: Tel is the abbreviation for telephone
Viv is a girl's name, short for Vivien

explanation.surface: Someone rings a girlfriend who lives abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is a major city in Israel, foreign from a British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Like a racehorse that's last in races — rotten!

indicators.note: take only the final letter of the word races

parts.note: an addled egg is a rotten one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a racehorse' wants a word about speed or form; it means fitted with a saddle.

clue.text: Journalist covers one religious festival

indicators.note: the outer word wraps round the inner letter, covering it

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A reporter covers a religious celebration.

clue.text: Where you'll see many a bumper trade event

definitions.text: Where you'll see many a bumper trade event

parts.words: Where you'll see many a bumper trade event
parts.note: bumper means a big event, but cars with their bumpers fill the field when people sell goods from their vehicles

explanation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is a market where people sell secondhand goods from the backs of their cars, a common British weekend event.

clue.text: Audacious leader's off in wood

parts.note: rash means recklessly bold, audacious

explanation.surface: A daring ringleader has fled into the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hardwood tree and the timber it yields.

clue.text: Period now to establish routine

parts.note: a day is a period of time
today means at the present time, now

explanation.surface: A spell of time now sets a pattern.

the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: trumpets belong to the brass section of an orchestra
HM stands for Her Majesty
